aspects.says: An assert is skipped unless the JVM runs with -ea; Surefire enables assertions for tests, so a check written as an assert passes the tests and is absent in production.
basis: section:An Assertion Checks Nothing Unless the JVM Runs with -ea

aspects.says: Checking arguments in the constructor (null, blank, range) throws while the code that holds the bad value is on the stack, so the trace names the caller.
basis: section:A Check in the Constructor Puts the Caller in the Trace

aspects.says: A constructor check on a list holds only if the object keeps its own copy: an unmodifiable view shows the caller's later changes, and List.copyOf copies and rejects null elements.
basis: section:A Check in the Constructor Puts the Caller in the Trace

aspects.says: An optional setting gets a default where a service running with it costs less than one refusing to start, as when a new release adds a key older config files lack; a setting with no safe value stays required.
basis: section:A Default Belongs Where Refusing to Start Costs More Than the Default

aspects.says: A null stored without a check fails later, in a stack trace that holds the frames of the code that used it and none of the code that stored it.
basis: section:A Null Stored Now Fails Later, in a Trace That Doesn't Name Who Stored It

aspects.says: A setting with no safe value stops the start when it is missing, instead of falling back to a guess.
basis: section:A Default Belongs Where Refusing to Start Costs More Than the Default

aspects.says: A misspelt key leaves the setting it was meant for at its default without any error; refusing keys the loader doesn't know turns the typo into a failed start.
basis: section:A Default Also Hides a Misspelt Key, Unless Unknown Keys Stop the Start

aspects.says: Refusing unknown keys makes an older release refuse a config file written for a newer one.
basis: section:A Default Also Hides a Misspelt Key, Unless Unknown Keys Stop the Start
aspects.reason: the cost shows only across two releases of a loader; the page states it as a consequence of the loader it shows, and one graded version of a loader cannot show a rollback

aspects.says: A value that doesn't parse is a failure, and a loader that catches it and uses the default hides it again.
basis: section:A Default Also Hides a Misspelt Key, Unless Unknown Keys Stop the Start

aspects.says: A value that is present but out of range fails nowhere: the code that uses it computes a wrong result.
basis: section:A Null Stored Now Fails Later, in a Trace That Doesn't Name Who Stored It
section:A Check in the Constructor Puts the Caller in the Trace
